title: vidIQ Automation Tools for YouTube Channels in 2026
summary: VidIQ automation automates research and optimization, but doesn't film or publish videos. See what desk work this tool actually handles.
body_markdown:
## VidIQ limits, errors, and fixes


Before you open a support ticket, find your failure among five categories. They cover nearly every vidIQ failure that stops an automation, and each has a fix you can try in minutes.


If the extension isn't showing, confirm it's enabled and pinned in your browser's extensions menu, then reload the YouTube tab. If it's still missing, reinstall it.


If the channel won't connect, sign in with the Google account that owns the channel, not a manager login, then reconnect.


When you hit a credit or plan limit, check your allowance in vidIQ's[credits-by-plan article](https://support.vidiq.com/en/articles/13928456-features-credits-by-plan) and either wait for the reset or move up a tier.


For stale data, refresh the page, then compare the number against YouTube Studio, which is the source of truth.


For billing or cancellation, search the[vidIQ Help Center](https://support.vidiq.com/) for the billing article before you act, and cancel ahead of the renewal date.


### VidIQ extension and channel connection problems


When the extension goes missing, it's usually a browser setting, not a vidIQ outage. Browsers hide new extensions inside a menu, so the toolbar icon is often simply collapsed.


If the channel won't connect, it's usually an account mismatch: you're signed in to a Google account that isn't the channel's owner. Fix the account first, because reconnecting repeatedly under the wrong login will fail every time.


### VidIQ plan limits and AI credits


Run out of AI credits and **a pipeline breaks silently** , much like an empty mapped field. Free gets[150 a month](https://support.vidiq.com/en/articles/13928456-features-credits-by-plan) , so a weekly titling workflow can run dry before the month ends and every later step fails.


If you're on an old subscription, don't expect it to match current tiers: the retired Pro plan had 1,000.


On Boost you get 2,000, enough for a daily research habit. Max has 6,000 credits a month against 150 on Free and the only sensible choice if several automated steps spend credits unattended.


Count the credits each automated step uses before you schedule it, and set a mid-month check so a dead allowance doesn't look like a broken workflow.


If a feature isn't listed in the credits article, ask vidIQ support whether it costs credits or needs a higher plan, and keep the written reply.


When data looks stale or mismatched, it's almost always a timing gap between vidIQ's snapshot and YouTube's live figures. Refresh first, then compare against YouTube Studio.


If the gap persists after a day, send support the video URL, the two numbers, and a screenshot with the time visible. A dated screenshot is the thing they can actually act on.
